results.name: Blind Eagle Deploys Fake UUE Files and Fsociety to Target Colombia's Judiciary, Financial, Public, and Law Enforcement Entities
results.description:
APT-C-36, also known as Blind Eagle, has been actively targeting organizations in Colombia and Ecuador since at least 2019. It relies on spear-phishing emails sent to specific and strategic companies to conduct its campaigns. On Feb. 20, the BlackBerry Research and Intelligence team witnessed a new campaign where the threat actor impersonated a Colombian government tax agency to target key industries in Colombia, including health, financial, law enforcement, immigration, and an agency in charge of peace negotiation in the country.

Based on the infector vector and payload deployment mechanism, we also uncovered campaigns targeting Ecuador, Chile, and Spain.

results.name: Phishing Attacks Against Ecuador
results.description: APT-C-36, also known as Blind Eagle, is an APT organization driven by economic interests. Since 2018, the group has been launching indiscriminate cyberattacks against citizens across South America. In a recent Blind Eagle campaign targeting Ecuadorian groups, researchers detected a new infection chain involving a more advanced toolset. Unlike the group's usual methods, the backdoor chosen for this attack is often used for espionage.

results.name: BlindEagle Targeting Ecuador With Sharpened Tools
results.description: An APT-C-36 group cyber-attack on Ecuador has been observed for the last few months, and the latest research by Check Point Research suggests that the group is developing a more advanced toolset.

results.name: APT-C-36 Updates Its Long-term Spam Campaign Against South American Entities With Commodity RATs
results.description: In 2019, we wrote a blog entry about a threat actor, likely based in Colombia, targeting entities in Colombia and other South American countries with spam emails. This threat actor is sometimes referred to as APT-C-36 or Blind Eagle. Since then, we have continued tracking this threat actor. In this blog entry, we share our new findings about APT-C-36’s ongoing spam campaign during that monitoring phase.

results.name: APT-C-36: Continuous Attacks Targeting Colombian Government Institutions and Corporations
results.description:
Since April 2018, an APT group (Blind Eagle, APT-C-36) suspected coming from South America carried out continuous targeted attacks against Colombian government institutions as well as important corporations in financial sector, petroleum industry, professional manufacturing, etc.

Till this moment, 360 Threat Intelligence Center captured 29 bait documents, 62 Trojan samples and multiple related malicious domains in total. Attackers are targeting Windows platform and aiming at government institutions as well as big companies in Colombia.
